title: Delayed Baggage? How to Handle Your Airport Pickup
description: Checked bag missing after landing? Report it to the airline, update your ride provider and agree on the pickup plan before leaving the terminal.
cta: Keep the bag report and the pickup plan connected.
image_alt: An empty curved black baggage carousel with brushed steel edges in a bright modern terminal.
body:
If a checked bag has not arrived, tell your ride provider promptly that you are still inside dealing with baggage, then follow the airline's reporting instructions. Agree on what happens to the pickup while you resolve the problem. A flight marked landed does not mean you are ready at the curb, and a missing bag does not automatically extend or cancel your car reservation.

Keep two conversations separate: the airline handles the bag; the transportation provider confirms the ride. You do not need to know when the bag will arrive before sending the first pickup update.

Contact the airline about the bag

SFO's baggage FAQ directs passengers to file a claim with their airline as soon as possible and follow up with that airline. The airport says it cannot access airline baggage-tracking systems. A bag that was checked for your flight is different from an item you left in the terminal.

Ask the airline which report or reference it will provide, how to check progress, and whether you should remain at the airport or arrange an onward handoff. Keep your bag identification receipt and the report details. The U.S. Department of Transportation's baggage guidance is the authoritative starting point for baggage reporting and passenger-rights questions; your chauffeur cannot determine the airline's obligations.

If you have an onward journey, tell the airline where you will actually be and when that location will change. Do not give a hotel address that will stop being useful after checkout. Confirm any delivery or collection arrangement directly with the airline; do not assume it is in place because a bag-tracking app shows a location.

Send a short pickup update while you are inside

Use the reservation or agreed day-of-trip contact, rather than submitting a second quote. Include enough information to connect the update to the correct traveler and ride:

  • Ride reference and traveler: identify the existing reservation.
  • Where you are: airport, terminal and baggage-service area or another clear indoor location.
  • Current situation: waiting for the belt, speaking with the airline, or completing a report.
  • Readiness: say whether you can leave now or whether the timing is still unknown.
  • Decision needed: ask the provider to confirm the pickup plan, next check-in and any applicable waiting or change terms.

Copyable message
Ride reference: [reference]. I have landed at [airport/terminal] but my checked bag has not arrived. I am [waiting for baggage / at the airline baggage desk] and am not ready for pickup. My departure time from the terminal is still uncertain. Please acknowledge this update and confirm the pickup arrangement, the next update time and any applicable waiting or change terms. My reachable contact is [number/channel].

Keep baggage tags, claim documents and personal travel information out of public posts. Share only the information the ride provider needs to coordinate the pickup.

Choose the next step from confirmed information

The airline asks you to keep waiting: update the provider and agree on another check-in. Do not promise a ready time based only on a possible delivery or another flight's estimated arrival.

The airline confirms you can leave: establish its bag-follow-up arrangement, then tell the ride provider that you are ready and follow the acknowledged pickup instructions. Report the luggage you actually have with you. A smaller load today does not confirm space for a later collection trip.

You may need a separate return to the airport: arrange that journey only after the airline confirms where and when collection can happen. Ask who must attend and what documents are required. Do not treat the original transfer as an open-ended collection service.

The group has different priorities: if some travelers want to leave while one person stays with the airline, tell the provider before splitting up. Confirm who rides, who remains the contact and what happens to the original booking. A second vehicle or extra stop needs its own confirmation.

Reconnect before walking to the curb

Send a final ready-to-leave message with your exact location. Follow the provider's airport-specific instructions; being outside does not make a pickup confirmed. At SFO, terminal curbs are for active loading, so a vehicle cannot simply wait there while a baggage problem is investigated.

If the flight or arrival airport also changed, use our flight-change checklist. If communications are unreliable, prepare the offline pickup fallback. Keep any later bag collection separate from your luggage and vehicle-fit brief.

For an existing Koast ride, use the contact on your reservation confirmation or the agreed day-of-trip contact and obtain acknowledgment. A new quote does not amend that ride. For a new journey, explore Koast airport transfers and include the confirmed flight, passengers and luggage in your quote request.
